questions.q: Which kind of question does the QBQ method recommend?
a: One that starts with what or how
One that starts with why or who
One that assigns blame to a colleague
One that waits for management to act
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the first step is asking what or how, which turns blame into ownership.

questions.q: What do incorrect questions tend to produce, according to the summary?
a: Blame, negativity and a lack of ownership
Clear plans and quick decisions
Better teamwork and lasting trust
Curiosity and open discussion
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the wrong questions as full of blame and a disturbing lack of ownership.

questions.q: Why should you include I in your questions?
a: It shifts focus from what you cannot change to what you can
It makes other people responsible for the outcome
It shows your manager that you are staying busy
It keeps the conversation polite and neutral
questions.why: Lesson 2 says using I moves attention from your limits to the parts you can improve.

questions.q: What does Miller say action brings, even when it leads to mistakes?
a: Learning and growth
Praise from managers
A guaranteed promotion
Fewer responsibilities
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that action brings learning and growth, while inaction brings stagnation.

questions.q: In the restaurant story, how does the waiter show accountability?
a: He buys a Diet Coke from a nearby store himself
He apologizes and offers a different brand
He asks his manager to place a special order
He explains that the restaurant only stocks Pepsi
questions.why: The overview describes him spending his own money to get the drink the customer wanted.
